name: GLKVM Cloud
description: GLKVM Cloud lets individuals and small businesses manage GL.iNet KVM devices remotely from their own server. It supports access-code onboarding, in-browser remote control, batch commands, and LDAP/OIDC sign-in, keeping data and bandwidth under your control.

app_vars.name: var_glkvm_access_ip
app_vars.label: Server Access IP
app_vars.help: Container IP by default; set the public IP when devices reach it over the internet

app_vars.name: var_glkvm_version
app_vars.label: Upstream Tag Pin
app_vars.help: Empty builds the latest tag; set e.g. v3.0.0 to pin or roll back

notes.text: Opening the platform by IP shows a browser certificate warning because GLKVM Cloud generates its own certificate on first start. Use your own domain and certificate to remove it.
The admin password is stored as RTTYS_PASS in /opt/glkvm-cloud-data/.env inside the container.

Allow ports 443, 10443, 5915 and 3478 (TCP and UDP) toward the container. TURN relay uses UDP 49160-49200, allow that range too behind NAT. Port 5912 serves only pre-v1.11 firmware (legacy token); block it once all devices use access codes. KVM devices need firmware v1.11.0 or later for access-code onboarding.
Before onboarding KVMs, triage each device for the CSA-2026-01 implant (gl-helper-triage.sh), factory-reset if indicated, and disable GoodCloud/AstroWarp on migrated devices.
